answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through random walks capped at a fixed horizon, so influence decays with path length rather than spreading without limit. A sybil cluster connected to honest identities by few edges has low conductance: its sparse boundary acts as a min-cut, limiting walk flow into the cluster and, under bounded transitivity, its aggregate voting weight. Like a lagoon divided from the ocean by a narrow inlet, internal density alone cannot create broad external trust.
